text:
maria: Quick heads-up — Acme POC failing when calling Private Endpoint through their corporate proxy, getting HTTP/403. Started at 09:02 PT.
acme-eng: Yep, we see 403 from the SDK but curl from our bastion -> private endpoint works fine.
alex: Can you paste a verbose curl from the app host? Curl + `-v` and `--resolve` if possible.
acme-eng: Here's reduced curl output:
```
* Connected to priv-endpoint.us-west-2.redwood.example.com (10.0.5.12) port 443
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
> GET /v1/engines HTTP/1.1
> Host: internal-proxy.local
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
```
samir: Aha — Host header is `internal-proxy.local`. Looks like their corporate proxy rewrites Host. Our backend validates host against the cert SAN and rejects unknown host.
maria: Is that expected with AWS PrivateLink/NLB fronting? Shouldn't SNI be the external name?
alex: SNI is set by client, but some proxies terminate TLS and re-initiate to the backend with a rewritten Host. Two options:
- Have their proxy preserve the original Host and SNI
- Or configure our Private Endpoint to accept the proxy's Host (not ideal)
samir: Quick mitigation: ask them to set `Host: redwood.example.com` in the app or use `curl --resolve 'redwood.example.com:443:10.0.5.12' -H 'Host: redwood.example.com'` to test.
acme-eng: Will try. Also capturing a tcpdump now: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/rdw.pcap` — sending when done.
ops-bot: POC-env:rdw-poc-42 created by deployer; cert rotation scheduled at 18:00 UTC.
maria: Thanks — if tcpdump shows TLS get terminated at proxy, we need them to open a pass-through or configure passthrough mode. I'll follow up on firewall/egress rules if tcpdump looks clean.
acme-eng: Update: after fixing proxy rule to forward Host and SNI, calls succeed. :tada:
alex: Great — marking as resolved for now. If they want, we can share a short doc on Host/SNI behaviour with Private Endpoints.
